title: Banned cards, blocks and new sets
goal: Know which cards you're allowed to play, and why that list changes.

steps.html: Not every card can be played in a tournament. Three things decide it: the Ban list, the Block rotation, and when a new set becomes tournament legal.

1. Banned cards. When a card makes games unfun or one deck takes over, Bandai bans it. A banned card can't be in your deck at all, in any art (alternate arts and parallels count too). Right now 6 cards are banned. The newest is Dracule Mihawk (OP14-020), the Green Leader that was the most played deck. It's been banned since October 12, 2026.

2. Banned pairs. Some cards are fine alone but too strong together. A Banned pair means you may play one or the other, never both in the same deck. Example: Luffy Leader OP11-040 can't be used with Charlotte Katakuri OP11-067.

3. Blocks. Look at the bottom corner of any card: there's a small number in a box. That's its block. Every April the oldest block leaves the Standard format. Until March 2027, Standard allows Blocks 2 to 5. Block 1 (sets OP-01 to OP-04 and the first 10 starter decks) is out, unless Bandai reprinted the card with a newer block number. Block 2 (OP-05 to OP-08) leaves in April 2027.

4. New sets. A new booster set comes out every few months. In English, a set is usually tournament legal a short time after its release. The next set is OP-18, The Dominance of God, out November 20, 2026. New sets are why the best decks keep changing.
You don't have to memorize any of this. Deckhand's deck builder checks the ban list for you and warns you about Block 1 cards. The Meta tab only counts tournament decks that are still legal.

quiz.q: Can you play an alternate-art copy of a banned card?
choices: No, every art of a banned card is banned
Only in casual games at a store event
quiz.why: A ban covers the card number, so every art and parallel is banned.

quiz.q: What does a banned pair mean?
choices: You can play only 2 copies of each
You can play one of them, but not both in the same deck
quiz.why: Each card is fine alone, but not together in one deck.

quiz.q: Which cards does Standard allow until March 2027?
quiz.why: Block 1 rotated out in April 2026. Blocks 2 to 5 are legal.
